Job Summary
We are seeking a Multi-Cloud Architect to design strategies, reference architectures, and platform capabilities that span multiple cloud providers — AWS, Azure, GCP, and selectively OCI — for enterprises operating on more than one cloud by deliberate choice. The role focuses on portability, abstraction layers, federated identity, cross-cloud networking, and platform offerings that hide cloud-specific complexity from product teams. The ideal candidate has architected meaningful multi-cloud capabilities, understands the trade-offs between portability and cloud-native depth, and brings strong opinions grounded in production experience.

Key Responsibilities
  • Define multi-cloud strategy, target-state architecture, and adoption guardrails across AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI as relevant.
  • Design federated identity, SSO, and cross-cloud authorization patterns that let workloads and engineers move between providers without compromising on least-privilege, auditability, or operational simplicity.
  • Architect cross-cloud networking including transit hubs, private connectivity, and zero-trust patterns.
  • Establish reusable infrastructure-as-code patterns that abstract cloud-specific implementations where appropriate.
  • Define container, Kubernetes, and serverless strategies that work consistently across providers.
  • Design data architecture strategies for cross-cloud data movement, residency, and analytics.
  • Drive multi-cloud observability, security monitoring, and unified policy enforcement, designing approaches that work consistently across providers and avoid the complexity of fragmented per-cloud tooling stacks.
  • Establish FinOps practices that operate consistently across multiple cloud providers.
  • Lead disaster recovery and business continuity strategies that span clouds.
  • Partner with security architects on multi-cloud security models, KMS strategies, and key management.
  • Provide guidance to engineering teams on when to use cloud-agnostic versus cloud-native patterns.
  • Produce high-quality architecture artifacts — context diagrams, sequence diagrams, decision records, and reference designs — that capture key technical decisions clearly enough to be understood months or years later.
  • Engage with cloud providers and partners to evaluate roadmap alignment.
  • Stay current with multi-cloud platform and tooling developments, regularly review release notes and community discussions, and translate noteworthy advances into concrete recommendations and adoption proposals for the team.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • Eight or more years of experience in cloud architecture roles.
  • Hands-on architecture experience across at least two major cloud providers.
  • Deep understanding of cloud networking, identity, and security across multiple providers.
  • Strong experience with infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code across clouds.
  • Experience designing federated identity and SSO across cloud platforms.
  • Solid understanding of Kubernetes, container platforms, and managed cloud services.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Multiple cloud certifications across providers.
  • Track record of leading multi-cloud architecture initiatives.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with abstraction platforms (Crossplane, Pulumi, Terraform CDK).
  • Familiarity with cloud-agnostic observability platforms.
  • Experience driving large-scale cloud-to-cloud migrations.
  • Exposure to regulated industries with multi-cloud mandates.
  • Public talks or writing on multi-cloud architecture.

jobs.title: Talent Acquisition Specialist
jobs.excerpt: ACU is affiliated with the Fellowship of the Church of Christ.
jobs.description:
ACU is affiliated with the Fellowship of the Church of Christ. This position requires the employee to be a professing Christian and willing to support the Christian mission of ACU.

‌

The Talent Acquisition Specialist serves as a strategic, full-cycle recruiting partner responsible for attracting, assessing, and hiring mission-aligned talent for faculty, academic staff, adjuncts, students, temporary employees, leadership, and other employee populations. The position partners with hiring managers, academic leaders, and search committees to clarify workforce needs, develop sourcing strategies, facilitate consistent selection processes, and deliver a professional and welcoming candidate experience.

The position supports ACU's evolving centralized, shared-services talent acquisition model by strengthening recruiting governance, standardizing hiring practices, improving Workday Recruiting workflows, and developing sustainable candidate pipelines. The role also connects recruitment with workforce planning, employer branding, compensation and offer processes, onboarding, employee integration, and broader employee flourishing initiatives across the ACU system.

This position has the potential to be on-site in Abilene, Texas, or remote.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1. Full-Cycle Recruitment and Hiring

  • Lead assigned searches from approved requisition through accepted offer and onboarding transition for faculty, academic, staff, adjunct, student, temporary, leadership, high-volume, hard-to-fill, and other positions.

  • Conduct intake meetings with hiring managers, academic leaders, and search committees to clarify position requirements, competencies, candidate profiles, sourcing strategies, timelines, and selection processes.

  • Create and manage requisitions, postings, approvals, candidate workflows, interview activity, dispositions, and offer documentation in Workday Recruiting.

  • Review applications and resumes against approved minimum and preferred qualifications, conduct structured phone or video screenings, and present qualified candidate slates with clear screening documentation.

  • Coordinate interviews, candidate communications, reference checks, background checks, employment verifications, and other required pre-employment activities.

  • Coordinate compensation and offer approvals with Talent Management and Total Rewards, and facilitate timely, professional offer communication and negotiation support.

  • Maintain timely communication with candidates and hiring stakeholders throughout the recruitment lifecycle.

2. Faculty, Academic, Staff, and Student Recruitment

  • Partner with Academic Affairs, deans, department chairs, and search committees on faculty, academic, adjunct, and other academic searches.

  • Support consistent search practices while respecting academic authority for evaluating credentials, discipline-specific qualifications, and academic selection decisions.

  • Support administrative, professional, operational, student, temporary, and other workforce recruitment across ACU divisions and locations.

  • Develop scalable recruiting approaches for recurring, high-volume, specialized, and difficult-to-fill positions.

  • Provide cross-functional recruiting coverage based on institutional priorities, workload, and business continuity needs.

3. Hiring Manager and Search Committee Partnership

  • Serve as a consultative recruiting partner to hiring managers and search committees throughout the hiring process.

  • Provide structured interview guides, evaluation tools, scorecards, and guidance on job-related candidate assessment and selection practices.

  • Assist departments with developing or updating position descriptions and translating workforce needs into clear qualifications and recruiting criteria.

  • Promote consistent hiring processes, approval requirements, documentation standards, and appropriate escalation of compliance, compensation, or selection concerns.

  • Build collaborative relationships across Human Resources, Academic Affairs, Finance, operational divisions, and campus leadership.

4. Talent Sourcing, Pipelines, and Employer Brand

  • Develop targeted sourcing strategies using professional networks, higher education resources, digital platforms, employee referrals, professional associations, churches, community organizations, and passive outreach.

  • Build and maintain talent pipelines for recurring, critical, leadership, and difficult-to-fill roles.

  • Represent ACU at selected job fairs, career events, professional gatherings, and recruiting activities.

  • Contribute to recruitment marketing, employment branding, and value-proposition initiatives that position ACU as a compelling, mission-centered employment destination.

  • Monitor labor-market conditions, sourcing effectiveness, and emerging talent gaps to inform recruiting and workforce-planning strategies.

5. Candidate Experience and Onboarding Partnership

  • Promote a candidate experience that reflects ACU’s Christian mission, institutional values, hospitality, professionalism, and commitment to employee flourishing.

  • Coordinate virtual and in-person recruiting activities and ensure candidates receive clear, timely, and respectful communication.

  • Facilitate a smooth transition from accepted offer to onboarding, orientation, integration, and employee-specific onboarding pathways.

  • Partner with HR Operations, onboarding and development leaders, Academic Affairs, and hiring departments to support effective new-hire transitions.

  • Identify and address candidate-experience gaps and recommend practical improvements.

6. Compliance, Documentation, and Hiring Governance

  • Apply university policies and established hiring requirements and support compliance with applicable federal and state employment laws.

  • Maintain complete, accurate, confidential, and auditable recruitment and selection records.

  • Promote consistent, job-related screening and selection practices and appropriate candidate disposition documentation.

  • Identify and escalate potential hiring, compensation, conflict-of-interest, records, or compliance concerns to the appropriate HR leader.

  • Support process standardization and governance across divisions, campuses, and employee populations.

7. Workday Recruiting and Systems Support

  • Use Workday Recruiting as the primary platform for requisition, candidate, interview, disposition, offer, and hiring workflow administration.

  • Support hiring managers and search committees in using Workday recruiting processes and employee or manager self-service practices.

  • Monitor workflows, data quality, approvals, and aging activity and resolve or escalate process issues.

  • Participate in Workday testing, optimization, reporting, automation, and system-enhancement initiatives affecting recruitment.

  • Maintain accurate candidate and recruiting data and support electronic records-management requirements.

8. Reporting, Workforce Planning, and Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor recruiting measures such as time-to-fill, requisition aging, candidate pipelines, source effectiveness, offer acceptance, and hiring activity.

  • Prepare recruiting dashboards, hiring reports, and workforce insights for HR and institutional leaders.

  • Identify recurring delays, process gaps, and opportunities to improve hiring quality, velocity, governance, and stakeholder experience.

  • Support workforce-planning discussions by identifying emerging hiring needs, labor-market trends, and talent risks.

  • Participate in talent acquisition projects, process improvement, policy development, cross-training, and business continuity planning.

  • Perform other duties as assigned that are consistent with the purpose and level of the position.

Supervisory Responsibilities

None. The position may coordinate search committees, recruiting vendors, temporary resources, career-event activities, or project teams without formal supervisory authority.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Communications, Organizational Leadership, Higher Education Administration, or a related field; equivalent relevant education and experience may be considered.

  • Three years of progressively responsible recruiting, talent acquisition, staffing, human resources, or related experience.

  • Experience managing multiple concurrent full-cycle recruitment processes.

  • Experience using an applicant tracking system or HR information system.

  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate candidates against documented qualifications and provide clear recommendations.

  • Strong communication, organization, project management, interpersonal, and customer-service skills.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and manage sensitive information professionally.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience recruiting in higher education, online education, a mission-driven organization, or a faith-based institution.

  • Experience supporting faculty, academic, staff, adjunct, student, high-volume, hard-to-fill, or leadership recruitment.

  • Workday Recruiting or Workday HCM experience.

  • Experience with structured interviews, search committees, talent sourcing, recruitment marketing, employment branding, or workforce planning.

  • Experience supporting a multi-campus, remote, or multi-state workforce.

  • SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, AIRS, or another relevant professional certification.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge

  • Full-cycle recruiting, talent sourcing, candidate pipeline development, and selection practices.

  • Higher education recruitment methods and faculty, adjunct, staff, and student hiring processes.

  • Applicant tracking systems, preferably Workday Recruiting.

  • Job-related candidate assessment, structured interviewing, recruiting documentation, confidentiality, and records-management practices.

  • Recruitment metrics, workforce planning, employment branding, and process improvement principles.

Skills and Abilities

  • Build credibility and productive relationships with candidates, hiring managers, academic leaders, search committees, and cross-functional partners.

  • Manage multiple searches, recurring deadlines, and shifting priorities with strong attention to detail and follow-through.

  • Develop sourcing strategies and qualified candidate pipelines for varied employee populations.

  • Communicate clearly and professionally in writing, by telephone, virtually, and in person.

  • Use recruiting data and systems to identify trends, improve workflows, and support decisions.

  • Balance strategic thinking, consultation, hospitality, and operational execution.

  • Work independently, exercise sound judgment, and maintain confidentiality and data integrity.

  • Adapt to changing organizational needs and support consistent practices across divisions and locations.

Core Competencies

  • Talent Acquisition and Candidate Assessment

  • Candidate Experience and Service Excellence

  • Relationship Building and Collaboration

  • Consultation, Communication, and Influence

  • Organization and Project Management

  • Sound Judgment and Confidentiality

  • Data and Technology Fluency

  • Process Improvement and Systems Thinking

  • Operational Excellence and Accountability

  • Mission Alignment and Cultural Stewardship

  • Hospitality and Candidate Care

  • Adaptability and Organizational Agility

Professional Development and Training

  • Ongoing training in Workday Recruiting, reporting, workflows, and applicable system enhancements.

  • Continuing education in recruiting practices, structured interviewing, hiring compliance, sourcing, employment branding, and workforce planning.

  • Training regarding ACU hiring policies, records management, data privacy, candidate experience, and mission-centered employment practices.

  • Professional development supporting higher education, faculty, leadership, multi-state, and specialized recruitment as assigned.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

  • Work is generally performed in an office, hybrid, or remote environment.

  • Extensive use of computers, video conferencing, telephone, applicant tracking systems, and recruiting technologies.

  • Ability to remain stationary for extended periods and perform detailed computer-based work.

  • Frequent interaction with candidates, employees, faculty, managers, search committees, and institutional leaders.

  • Occasional travel between ACU locations and to recruiting events may be required, including limited overnight travel.

  • Occasional evenings or weekend participation may be required for interviews, recruiting events, or priority searches.

  • Ability to communicate clearly in person, virtually, in writing, and by telephone, and to work effectively under pressure.

  • Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals to perform the essential functions.

Time Demands

The position must remain responsive during priority searches, high-volume recruiting periods, academic hiring cycles, and other critical institutional staffing needs. Work schedules may require occasional flexibility to support candidate availability, interviews, recruiting events, and time-sensitive hiring decisions.

ACU does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, age, sex, disability, genetic information, national or ethnic origin in employment opportunities, in keeping with applicable state and federal law.

ACU is committed to maintaining a safe and secure campus environment and protecting the university's financial and physical assets. Therefore, Abilene Christian University conducts background checks on all candidates for employment in security sensitive positions. As a current employee, it will be determined if you need an additional background check upon your hire.

About the team

The Agentic AI team at Zillow is at the forefront of transforming the real estate industry by helping millions of people use AI technologies to find their next home. We aim to redefine the home shopping and transaction experience by providing an always-on assistant that integrates deep user insights and sophisticated reasoning. By embedding domain knowledge and specialized expertise in these assistants, we empower home buyers and real estate professionals to gain efficiency while maintaining Zillow's competitive edge. This lean, customer-focused team comprises scientists and engineers working together to deliver a delightful customer experience. We strongly believe in accountability, collaboration, and transparency.

About the role

Zillow is looking for a Principal Machine Learning Engineer on the Agentic AI team to develop advanced multimodal foundational technologies. They will be hands-on in prototyping ideas, evaluating, and deploying models to Zillow's highly scalable infrastructure platforms. They’ll be developing perception and language understanding, deep reasoning, and reinforcement learning to handle AI agent decision-making.

As a Principal Machine Learning Engineer on the Agentic AI team, you will:

  • Leverage frameworks like AgentSDK, and LangChain/LangGraph to design, prototype, and develop multi-agent systems that are capable of highly autonomous and context-aware interactions

  • Leverage advanced GenAI models including reasoning models, real-time voice API, etc, to build agentic prototypes and later on convert them into product-level agentic skills and deploy to users.

  • Have the mentality of “build, learn, and pivot”, and hold the high bar of shipping into production.

  • Mentor and guide engineers in using the right technologies for agentic AI solutions and foster a culture of innovation and responsible AI usage

  • Distill complex research findings and system designs into actionable insights for diverse audiences—including executives

  • Remain on the cutting edge of agentic AI emerging paradigms, driving product innovation

  • Serve as the focal point for applied science projects, driving alignment on timelines, and prioritization

  • Continuously refine processes for experimentation, A/B testing, and production rollouts to balance rapid innovation with reliability and responsible deployment.

This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $204,400.00 - $326,600.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $194,200.00 - $310,200.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

As a Principal Machine Learning Engineer, you are a roll-up-the-sleeves and get-it-done engineer who can marry state-of-the-art technology (i.e., LLM models, either from OpenAI or open source) with large-scale engineering. We are looking for someone who has:

  • A master's degree or above, equivalent experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with emphasis on foundational LLM, agentic AI, reinforcement learning, AI planning, or natural language processing

  • 7+ years of hands-on work building large-scale, high-impact solutions—ideally in the most recent two years building agent-based systems, multi-agent collaboration, or similar paradigms

  • Experience developing dialogue systems capable of long conversations, multi-step reasoning, context-rich decision-making

  • Experience deploying and scaling AI services capable of handling hundreds of millions of daily interactions with high availability, low latency, and robust fault tolerance

  • A track record of publishing high-impact research in top AI/ML venues is a big plus.

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help customers navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company that's reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.

Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the country. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2025, and included on the PEOPLE Companies That Care® 2025list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.

No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewAt Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

The Motorola Solutions’ CommandCenter Software Customer Success Team empowers our customers to identify and unleash the full power of their CommandCenter Software products and services.

We build relationships with agencies by leveraging data-driven insights to understand their most urgent needs. We are committed to consistent delivery and follow-through at scale, ensuring every agency—regardless of size—is equipped to serve their communities in the moments that matter.


Job Description

In this full-time role, you will serve as a Scaled Customer Success Associate who works with new and existing Public Safety clients to ensure a smooth adoption, maximize usage, value, and product satisfaction. As a Scaled Customer Success Associate, you will be the engine behind our "one-to-many" strategy, ensuring our customers fully adopt and realize the value of our technology as soon as possible. Your mission is to help existing agencies find the solutions to the challenges that prevent them from being successful with our solutions and that might risk their retention. Unlike traditional CSM roles that manage a small book of business, you will leverage automation, data analytics, and high-impact content to support hundreds of agencies simultaneously. Your mission is to democratize expertise, making sure every customer, regardless of size, has the tools they need to save lives and serve their communities effectively.

Responsibilities:

  • Full-Lifecycle Management:Own the customer journey for a high-volume portfolio, ensuring agencies are successful from initial go-live through their renewal cycles.

  • Data-Driven Health Monitoring:Regularly analyze usage data to identify accounts that are "unhealthy" (low usage) or "at-risk." Coordinate with our Content strategy team to execute scaled digital outreach campaigns to re-engage these users and drive adoption.

  • Process Trailblazing: Help build and refine the "Scaled" operating model—finding the hidden patterns, coming up with creative ways to address our customer’s challenges and developing the most efficient ways to provide support and education to a high volume of agencies through technology.

  • Content Creation & Self-Service Enablement:Develop video and easy-to-digest self-service resources, including "How-to" videos, and best practice guides that can be used by our customers when needed. Translate complex technical workflows into simple, actionable content tailored for Motorola’s customer base.

  • Community Forum Management:Monitor and create content to address customer questions and to keep the conversation going. Enable the forum to be a resource hub where users can share insights and learn from peer successes.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • The Scaled Mindset: You enjoy finding ways to solve a problem once and sharing it with a thousand people, rather than solving the same problem a thousand times.

  • Experience: 3+ years of experience in a customer-facing role in customer advocacy, sales or public safety.

  • Systems & Process Oriented: You enjoy finding the most efficient way to accomplish a goal and you’re not afraid of working with data to find patterns or to gather actionable insights.

  • Communication:Ability to communicate clearly and effectively with customers, peers and leadership with a strong emphasis on written communication

  • Technical Aptitude: Demonstrated ability to quickly learn complex software and translate technical features into simple, value-based recommendations.

  • Time Management: Exceptional ability to prioritize a high volume of tasks and manage a large portfolio of customers without letting details fall through the cracks.

  • Relationship Builder:Demonstrated ability to influence and maintain working relationships in large, cross-functional organizations and law enforcement agencies.

  • Team Player: Ability to coordinate and collaborate effectively with cross-functional internal resources to find the solution and the support the customer needs as soon as possible.

  • Strong Customer Focus: Demonstrate understanding of the customer needs, proactively responding and following through on customer commitments.

  • Adaptability and Flexibility:Ability to adjust to new situations, be uncomfortable in the unknown and take initiative.

  • Rave portfolio product knowledge preferred.

Target Base Salary Range: $70,000 - $80,000 USD

Consistent with Motorola Solutions values and applicable law, we provide the following information to promote pay transparency and equity. Pay within this range varies and depends on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The actual offer will be based on the individual candidate.


Basic Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree & 3+ years of experience in a Customer-Facing role, Sales or Public Safety

  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. indefinitely is required. Employer work permit sponsorship is not available for this position.


Travel Requirements

Under 10%

None

Experienced

Yes

Motorola Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer.   • Direct cross-functional prioritization and delivery processes to ensure cohesive, timely outcomes

  • Champion transparency and communication of data technology roadmaps across the organization

Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Champion capability development in cloud engineering, Databricks, CI/CD, SQL, and Python

Experience & Track Record

  • Exposure to Real World Data in the clinical/medical space

  • Experience with GxP regulations in a life sciences environment advantageous

  • Deep experience leading teams in data delivery management and execution, including major projects in data management, data integration, and analytics

    • Successfully developing and implementing applications in new computing architecture environments using innovative technologies

    • Managing technical personnel across multiple project lifecycle phases with cross-functional experience

    • Managing financial resources to achieve goals across multiple projects

    • Developing efficient and effective solutions to complex business challenges

Technical Expertise

  • Extensive experience implementing and supporting enterprise data initiatives on cloud platforms

  • Demonstrated expertise in data and cloud platforms, particularly Azure Databricks

  • Significant experience with medallion architecture-based data lake implementations

  • Proficiency in modern data management and data-sharing tools, programming languages (especially Python), relational databases, data transformation, and development frameworks

  • Deep understanding of architectural best practices, application design, and estimation processes

Education

In return we will be able to offer you a structured career pathway and encouragement to develop within the role including awareness and understanding of the industry. jobs.excerpt: Compensation for this role is expected to be approximately $114,000 annually.
jobs.description:
Compensation for this role is expected to be approximately $114,000 annually.

R1 is the leading provider of technology-driven solutions that transform the patient experience and financial performance of hospitals, health systems, and medical groups. We are the one company that combines the deep expertise of a global workforce of revenue cycle professionals with the industry’s most advanced technology platform, encompassing sophisticated analytics, AI, intelligent automation, and workflow orchestration.

As our Clinical Documentation Improvement (CDI) Specialist, you will use clinical and coding knowledge for conducting clinically based concurrent and retrospective reviews of inpatient medical records. Every day, you will evaluate the documentation of clinical services by identifying opportunities for improving the quality of medical record documentation, including focused reviews in areas identified by CDI leadership: Mortality reviews, PSI reviews, and other identified projects. Facilitates and obtains appropriate physician documentation for any clinical conditions or procedures to support the appropriate severity of illness, expected risk of mortality, and complexity of care of the patient. Participates in ongoing documentation improvement initiatives, including formal and informal education plans related to clinical documentation improvement to providers and the CDI team.

To thrive in this role, you must have the following knowledge:

  • Highly skilled in CDI practices, coding, and documentation requirements related to quality outcomes, evaluation of medical record data for accuracy and reimbursement; self-motivated to stay abreast of CMS rules and regulations and incorporate those changes into daily practice.

  • Front Line CDI experience in an acute care hospital

  • Have an active RN license with experience in: ICU, Med surge, telemetry, or ED.

Here’s what you will experience working as a Clinical Documentation Improvement (CDI) Specialist:

  • Initiates physician interaction when ambiguous, missing, or conflicting information is in the medical record, through the physician query process and/or participation in rounding with the physicians by requesting additional documentation for correct coding and compliance necessary for accurate reflection of CMI, LOS, and optimal resource utilization.

  • Educates physicians and other staff on documentation requirements, coding guidelines, and reimbursement policies

  • Utilizes Hospital coding code set, policies and procedures, Federal and State coding reimbursement guidelines, and application of the Coding Clinic Guidelines to assign working DRG, reviewing patient records throughout hospitalization that have been identified as focus DRG by regulatory agencies or the facility to ensure the codes are reported at the highest specificity.

  • Collaborates with coders, auditors, quality improvement teams, and other stakeholders to resolve documentation issues and improve coding accuracy

  • Stays updated on the latest developments and changes in clinical documentation standards, coding rules, and regulatory requirements

  • Conducts focused reviews in areas identified by CDI leadership: Mortality reviews, PSI reviews, as well as other identified projects

Required Qualifications

  • Associate’s Degree in Nursing (Bachelor’s Degree in Nursing is preferred)

  • An active US RN license is required

  • Must have front line CDI experience in an acute care hospital

  • Three to five years of recent clinical work experience in the medical-surgical area, ICU, telemetry, and or emergency department

  • Knowledge or experience in electronic medical records (EMR) platforms and CDI platforms

For this US-based position, the base pay range is $52,025.00 - $97,528.69 per year . Individual pay is determined by role, level, location, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.This job is eligible to participate in our annual bonus plan at a target of 5.00%

We go beyond expectations in everything we do. Not only does that drive customer success and improve patient care, but that same enthusiasm is applied to giving back to the community and taking care of our team — including offering a competitive benefits package.

jobs.description:
Position Title: VP of Engineering

Reports to: CEO (interim)

Location: UK, Remote

Contract Type: Full-Time, Permanent

About BibliU

BibliU is an award-winning, technology-led B2B company transforming the $65bn educational content industry. With a 90% CAGR the past 5 years, we are just getting started. We've cracked the code on Day 1 access to affordable digital course materials for students, while delivering comprehensive campus store solutions that foster human relationships, and increase our stickiness in the world of AI.

The result? Measurable impact: 10% higher student retention, 1-point GPA increases, and partnerships with 170 universities serving 600,000 students each year.

We've fundamentally changed how universities procure, distribute, and manage learning content. We partner with 4,000+ publishers, including Pearson, Oxford University Press, and Wiley to deliver content to universities, and provide rich engagement data and interactive tools like quizzes that help students actually learn.

Here's what makes our story compelling:

Founded in late 2015 as an Oxford University spin out, we've grown explosively with 90% CAGR over the last five years, including 65% in FY25, reaching $100m in annual revenue. Our Series B raised $23m led by Nesta Impact Investments (with Guinness Asset Management, Stonehage Fleming, and Oxford Sciences Enterprises). In late 2023, we acquired Texas Book Company (now 'BibliU Campus') to become the only fully vertically integrated player in the market, driving US organic growth which now represents 90% of our business.

We're hungry for more. We're actively building our M&A pipeline as we compete head-to-head against legacy bricks-and-mortar providers to improve the faculty and student experience while boosting the financial sustainability of universities.

Our culture is collaborative, high-growth, and agile. You’ll join an experienced and motivated executive team with backgrounds from Instructure (Canvas) and other successful edtech companies with exit experience. We operate as a distributed team across the UK and US, with offices in London.

Role Overview

BibliU is hiring a VP Engineering to lead and grow its engineering function. This role owns team leadership, engineering standards, technical governance, security posture, and delivery against the product roadmap.

The engineering organisation today is about 15 engineers across application and platform, primarily full stack TypeScript on AWS, with 1-2 managers but otherwise a fairly flat team structure. You'll inherit a function that has been through a period of change, and is in the middle of changing how software gets built.

The first six months are about earning the team's trust, getting delivery predictable, and landing AI-assisted development as a standard part of how the team works rather than scattered individual use. Beyond that, this is a build job: growing the team as the business grows, setting the architecture direction for the next stage, and taking BibliU's platform from $100m revenue to what comes after.

It is expected that product and engineering will sit under a single leader longer term, so you'll spend your time on engineering rather than on cross-functional alignment.

What Success Looks Like in year one

  • The team is stable, growing, and the engineering managers are developing under you.
  • Security posture is documented, owned and defensible, and customer security reviews are routine rather than fire drills.
  • Availability, performance and incident metrics are improving.
  • Delivery is predictable, with an honest roadmap and a release process the team trusts.
  • AI-assisted development is measurably in use across the team, under agreed review and quality standards, with quality and security metrics improved against the baseline set in month one.
  • Multiple engineering workflows have materially changed, with the before/after evidenced.
  • Engineering standards, architecture decisions and technical debt are documented, and there's a credible architecture plan for the next stage of scale.

What We Are Looking For

Must have

  • Significant experience leading software engineering or application development functions at VP, Director or CTO level.
  • A track record of leading teams through change.
  • Demonstrated accountability for delivery of complex web and mobile applications, including release governance.
  • Experience managing engineering teams and technical leads.
  • Full stack TypeScript and AWS experience is required.
  • Track record of owning application security: secure coding practice, vulnerability management, audit and customer security review.

Good to have

  • Experience implementing development governance, DevOps practice, CI/CD and quality assurance standards.
  • Proven ability to manage technical risk and align engineering output with commercial objectives, and to report both credibly to senior leadership.
  • Strong understanding of cloud-native architecture and modern development frameworks.
  • A considered, practical position on AI-assisted development: tooling, guardrails, review, and how to measure real gains.
  • Experience in SaaS, EdTech, FinTech or other product-led digital environments.
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity standards and secure coding practices, and of the certifications customers ask about.
  • Familiarity with international product deployments and multi-region infrastructure.
  • Exposure to data-driven product optimisation and analytics frameworks.
  • Experience in a resource-constrained scale-up, where pragmatism and sequencing matter more than ideal solutions.

Benefits

Our benefits are all aimed at supporting a healthy work-life balance and cultivating a company culture where you can bring your whole, human self to work.

Here's what we offer:

  • 🌴 35 days holiday per year (excluding public holidays!) - yep, that’s not a typo!
  • 🎂 Your birthday off.
  • 🌱 12 scheduled company wellness Fridays off per year.
  • ❤️ Enhanced maternity & paternity allowance.
  • ⏰ Flexible working hours - we’re a remote team spread across the US and UK.
  • 💻 Work-from-home allowance to help you set up your dream WFH station.
  • 🚴 Cycle-to-work scheme (UK).
  • 🛟 Life Insurance up to 4 x salary .
  • ❤️ Private health insurance.
  • 👁️ Annual eye test and up to £100 towards frames for glasses required for DSE work.

We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds, experiences and identities to apply. Each new hire is an opportunity for us to bring in a different perspective and BibliU is committed to building an inclusive and supportive workplace where everyone can do rewarding work.

Please note: We do not work with external recruiters/recruitment agencies. This position will be filled directly by BibliU and we kindly request that external recruiters/recruitment agencies refrain from submitting candidates for this role.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Where you sit.

You'll be joining the Origination stream, the product area responsible for the end-to-end mortgage journey, covering self-serve and advisor-supported application flows, underwriting, decisioning, and funding.

This is a Senior PM role where part of your mandate is to help shape and own your specific substream within origination. You'll work closely with the stream lead, and together you'll define the boundaries of your focus area based on your strengths, the team's needs, and where the biggest opportunities are. It's a rare chance to have real influence over your own scope from day one.

Your closest collaborators will be engineering teams building on Nesto Cloud, mortgage operations and underwriting experts who live inside these processes daily, and the brokers and advisors who depend on these tools to serve clients.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Act as one of the primary origination subject-matter experts for your substream, deeply understanding end-to-end origination processes, regulatory requirements, and operational realities.
  • Define and own the product vision, roadmap, and feature prioritization for your area, ensuring it reflects real-world origination requirements, operational efficiencies, and compliance considerations.
  • Identify and assess the impact of new lending features, regulatory changes, and origination workflow evolutions to help shape product direction and support strategic decisions.
  • Work closely with engineering, design, QA, operations, and compliance to validate designs and proposed solutions, ensuring they align with origination best practices and industry standards.
  • Support the backlog refinement process by prioritizing origination-related epics and stories, balancing customer experience, operational needs, and technical feasibility.
  • Participate in release planning, UAT, and pre-launch readiness to ensure origination use cases are fully supported, edge cases are addressed, and downstream impacts are understood.
  • Conduct research on industry trends, evolving regulations, origination technologies, and competitor approaches, bringing insights to guide product evolution.
  • Create and maintain detailed documentation of origination processes, scenarios, requirements, and system behaviours to support product teams and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Act as the go-to expert for your origination workflows, answering questions, supporting issue triage, and ensuring the product supports exceptional origination experiences across all lending products.

AI-Augmented Ways of Working

  • Actively use AI tools (Cursor, Claude, Figma AI, Gemini, and others) to accelerate your PM workflow from discovery through delivery: synthesizing research, prototyping ideas, and measuring results.
  • Don't wait for a perfect process to test a hypothesis. Use the tools available to you to get to answers faster, whether that means building a rough prototype, running a quick experiment, or drafting a solution to pressure-test with users before it becomes a roadmap item.
  • Comfortable going beyond traditional PM boundaries when the situation calls for it, the best people here don't hand off and wait, they stay close to the work and use every tool at their disposal to move it forward.
  • Stay ahead of how AI is reshaping mortgage origination and bring informed recommendations to the roadmap.
  • Share what you discover. How you work should make the people around you better.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The profile.

  • 5-7+ years of hands-on experience in product management, ideally with exposure to mortgage origination, lending, or a closely adjacent regulated financial services environment.
  • Understanding of end-to-end origination functions from application flows, document collection, underwriting, credit decisioning to compliance checkpoints, and funding processes.
  • Knowledge of regulatory and compliance requirements related to mortgage and consumer lending, including provincial regulations, OSFI guidelines, insurance requirements, and reporting obligations.
  • Experience working with origination platforms, LOS systems, or lending technology, with the ability to translate operational needs into functional system requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with product, engineering, design, operations, compliance, and QA teams.
  • Exceptional problem-solving skills with an ability to anticipate downstream impacts and foresee edge cases in origination workflows.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex origination concepts clearly to non-experts in Product and Engineering.
  • Proven, active fluency with AI tools across your PM workflow : discovery, testing, documentation, analysis, and measurement. We will ask you specifically how you use them.

PREFERRED BUT NOT A MUST

  • Experience with other lending products such as HELOC, personal loans, private lending, reverse mortgages, or construction financing.
  • Familiarity with broker and advisor-facing workflows and the nuances of supported versus self-serve client journeys.
  • Exposure to AI or ML-assisted decisioning, document intelligence, or automation in a financial services context.

YOU SHOULDN'T APPLY IF
Be honest with yourself.

  • You're only comfortable in a well-defined product area. This role requires you to help shape your own scope: ambiguity is the starting condition, not an exception.
  • You treat AI tools as a curiosity rather than a daily accelerant.
  • You hand off a PRD and consider your job done. Ownership here runs from discovery all the way through to measuring results in production.
  • You don't thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, and sometimes ambiguous environment.
  • You are not open to experimentation and continuous improvement.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

How we get to know each other.

  • Recruiter Screen – 30 minutes
  • Discovery Call with Director of Product – 30 minutes
  • Take-home Assignment followed by Presentation and Q&A – 60 minutes
  • Final Stakeholder Interview – 45 minutes
  • Criminal Record and Reference Checks + Offer

Why You'll Love Working Here

We believe great people do their best work when they're supported professionally, personally, and financially. That's why we offer a comprehensive rewards package designed to help you thrive at every stage of your career.

  • Competitive Rewards — Competitive compensation, performance incentives (where applicable), and recognition for your contributions.
  • Health & Wellness — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, Health & Wellness Spending Accounts (where applicable), telemedicine, Employee Assistance Programs, and mental health support for you and your family.
  • Time to Recharge — Generous vacation (4 weeks), floater days, and statutory holidays to help you recharge.
  • Planning for the Future — RRSP matching to support your long-term financial wellbeing.
  • Family Support — Enhanced maternity and parental leave top-up programs.
  • Learning & Growth — Education assistance, mentorship, training, and opportunities to build your career across Nesto Group.
  • Tools for Success — Modern technology, collaborative teams, and the resources you need to do your best work.


Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At Nesto Group, we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to succeed.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis), persons with disabilities, members of racialized communities, women, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

If you require accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process, we are committed to working with you to meet your needs.

jobs.description:
Government Employees Health Association, Inc. The QAE/DevOps Solutions Architect leads the design and implementation of enterprise-scale quality engineering, automation, and DevOps capabilities. This role will define end-to-end SDLC and QA architecture with a strong emphasis on Azure DevOps pipelines, CI/CD integration, governance, quality gates, and AI-assisted quality engineering practices. The QAE/DevOps Solutions Architect leads the evolution from manual testing to a Quality Assurance Engineering (QAE) function using data to drive to enterprise outcomes.

SKILLS

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Define QAE and DevOps automation architecture. Define and evolve the test technology stack, document the reference architecture, code standards, and repo structure the team builds against.
  • Stay up to date on emerging technology in the Quality and DevOps space. Assess how new technologies can be leveraged to enhance quality services. Stay up to date on the quality implications for emerging technology in development, data, and analytical domains.
  • Help lead and assist with the modernization of the end-to-end SDLC process and ensure our process and supporting technology stack aligns with emerging best practices.
  • Design, implement, and optimize Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines with integrated quality gates and governance controls. Establish enterprise standards for build, release, and deployment pipelines, including compliance and auditability.
  • Integrate automated testing frameworks into CI/CD pipelines (UI, API, performance, data validation). Define and enforce QA governance models, including standards, controls, and best practices across teams.
  • Participate in the automation backlog, consuming risk-ranked regression suites with a deliberate record of which test cases are automated and why. Identify and retire technical debt in the QA technology stack.
  • Lead adoption of AI-assisted QA tools (e.g., test generation, defect prediction, intelligent automation).
  • Partner with DevOps, engineering, and platform teams to ensure seamless end-to-end SDLC integration. Lead shift-left quality initiatives to embed testing early in the development lifecycle and shift-right processes to ensure learnings with Production incidents.
  • Evaluate and select tools and frameworks for QA automation, pipeline optimization, and AI integration.
  • Mentor QA and DevOps engineers on best practices for automation, pipelines, and governance.
  • Drive continuous improvement of deployment reliability, speed, and quality metrics.
  • Extend QA oversight onto AI agents and bot interactions, define rules/grades for bots and ensure parity of quality controls across human and virtual agents.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

You'll also provide counseling about insurance needs and product availability. You'll specialize in personal lines (auto, home, boats, motorcycles, recreational vehicle, umbrellas, flood) business.

jobs.excerpt: Futures start here.  Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born.
jobs.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with theGallup Exceptional Workplace Award, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At KinderCare Learning Companies, you’ll use your skills and expertise to support the work (and fun) that happens in our sites and centers every day. From marketers and strategists to financial analysts and data engineers, and so much more, we’re all passionate about crafting a world where children, families, and organizations can thrive.

As Senior Databricks Engineer, you will be a hands-on technical expert and force multiplier on our Databricks-based data platform. You’ll own the design, optimization, and governance of our medallion lakehouse architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold), the Unity Catalog, and the pipelines that feed enterprise BI and emerging AI/ML products. You'll operate deep in the Databricks ecosystem daily (Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Workflows, Delta Live Tables / Lakeflow, MLflow) while also shaping how the platform supports next-generation capabilities, including Databricks-native ML/AI features such as Genie spaces, feature engineering, model serving, and vector search. This role partners closely with the Data Engineering Lead and BI Architect and sits in a SOX-governed environment, so a strong instinct for data governance, access control, and auditable engineering practices is essential.

Responsibilities:

Platform & Pipeline Engineering

  • Design, build, and optimize production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines across the medallion architecture using Delta Lake, Delta Live Tables / Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, and Databricks Workflows

  • Own performance tuning and cost efficiency across the platform — cluster/job sizing, Photon, partitioning and Z-ordering, Liquid Clustering, Auto Loader, and DBU cost governance

  • Architect and enforce data models that support enterprise BI (Microsoft Fabric/Power BI) and downstream analytics products

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for Databricks assets (Databricks Asset Bundles, Repos, Git-based deployment) following Agile and Test-Driven Development practices

  • Integrate platform pipelines with middleware and source systems (e.g., Boomi) and cloud-native services

Governance, Security & Reliability

  • Administer and evolve Unity Catalog: catalogs/schemas, fine-grained access control, lineage, row/column-level security, and workspace-catalog bindings

  • Implement and enforce data quality, observability, and reliability practices (expectations/constraints, monitoring, alerting, SLA management) across pipelines

  • Partner with security, compliance, and audit teams to maintain SOX ITGC alignment; access reviews, change control, and auditable engineering practices

Many of our systems are designed around the APCO Project 25 communications standard. With the growth of data services some of our customer’s mobile wireless networks are being enhanced with LTE infrastructure for applications such as APX Next Smart and live mobile video transmission supplementing our traditional core voice and narrowband data networks.


Job Description

NOTE: This position is Remote + Travel. Candidates must reside in Georgia, North Carolina or South Carolina.

The Systems Engineer will be responsible for the public safety design and implementation of solutions for Motorola’s ASTRO 25 and adjacent technologies for State and Local government agencies. We are looking for Engineers who are energized by delivering solutions that truly make a difference. Note: This is a remote position with travel (25-50%) to support projects in T4E sub territory.

Projects are varied in scope, ranging from a single-site installation for a local municipality, to a complex statewide public safety communications system costing tens or hundreds of millions of dollars. The team comprises Sales, Project Management and System Engineering personnel working together in a high performance culture, often with demanding cycle times and high customer expectations because we are working on mission critical communication systems.

Engineer of Record Project Responsibilities:

The Systems Engineer will work with a field team of Project Management, Systems Engineers, System Technologists, Construction Managers, and Customer Service Managers, and will be responsible for leading technical aspects of the assigned project until system acceptance.

This involves:

  • Design and implementation of the radio network including infrastructure, subscribers, mobile backhaul and WAN and CEN networks.

  • High level of customer and consultant interaction involving customer design reviews, customer witnessed staging and acceptance testing events, coverage acceptance testing, live system upgrades, and troubleshooting efforts.

  • System buildout, configuration and acceptance testing in both lab staging and field environments

  • Radio coverage testing, frequency analysis and interference mitigation

  • Radio system licensing (FCC/Industry)

  • Preparation of system fleet map, encryption and radio programming templates

  • Complete system documentation

  • Live system cutovers and upgrades

Additional Skills/Knowledge:

  • Radio Frequency Engineering principles

  • Land / Mobile Radio Engineering principles

  • RFDS principles to include antenna and cable selection, transmit combiners, receive multi-couplers, and lightning protection systems.

  • P25 Land Mobile Radio terminology and two-way subscriber radio provisioning methods.

  • Experience with Motorola ASTRO 25 architecture is a plus.

  • Servers and related systems to include: VMware ESXI, Linux, and Microsoft operating systems.

  • Construction of remote communication sites to include: site selection, grounding, compound development, tower and shelter requirements.

  • Fortinet and Juniper firewalls, Nokia 7705 series routers, Juniper SRX/MX (Junos) series routers, HP/Aruba and Juniper switches

  • Remote access using SSH, SCP, SFTP, RDP

  • Knowledge with point-to-point Microwave systems, Microwave RF & Network design

  • FCC licensing and frequency search

  • Software applications integration, Application Protocol Interfaces (API) concepts, computer operating systems, and the OSI model.

  • Networking protocols and devices including RSVP-TE, OSPF, ISIS, BGP, MPLS, SIP, RTP, SNMP, NAT, routers, switches, and stateful packet firewalls.

  • Knowledge of physical layer such as fiber, copper, and microwave.

  • Knowledge of IP networking, network design methodologies & troubleshooting (Ethernet, TCP/IP, L2/L3, MPLS).

  • Certifications a plus through CompTIA Network+, Juniper JNCIA-Junos, Nokia NRS1, CCNA or similar a plus.

  • Works collaboratively and builds relationships with other colleagues, customers, and third party service professionals.

jobs.description:
The Team Lead, Operations Account Management is responsible for day‑to‑day operational performance and execution for assigned clients, serving as the primary operations liaison between client facilities and internal delivery teams. This role focuses on tactical revenue cycle outcomes, ensuring accurate reporting, effective communication, and consistent execution across billing, follow‑up, collections, denials, and claim resolution workflows.

This position is accountable for operational monitoring and client relationship management. The Team Lead translates client needs into clear operational priorities, monitors key performance indicators, identifies risks and trends, and supports timely issue resolution to protect cash, A/R performance, and client satisfaction.

The role also provides operational mentorship to staff by reinforcing daily best practices, supporting training and performance efforts, and helping remove execution barriers. Success is measured by client retention, escalation volume, and core revenue cycle performance indicators.

These Goals and objectives are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed; employees will be required to perform other job-related duties as required. Goals and objectives are subject to change.

All activities must be in compliance with Equal Employment Opportunity laws, HIPAA, ERISA and other regulations, as appropriate.

Essential Functions: In addition to meeting performance expectations, this role includes the following specific responsibilities:

Discrete Responsibilities (Primary Accountability)

  • Operational Performance Monitoring: Monitor daily operational performance, battle cards, action plans, and key KPIs for assigned clients, including A/R days, cash performance, denial trends, and accuracy measures.
  • Primary Operations Liaison: Act as the primary operational point of contact between clients and internal delivery teams, ensuring timely, accurate, and consistent communication.
  • Operational Translation: Translate client needs, issues, and requests into actionable operational priorities and execution plans.
  • Risk & Trend Identification: Identify operational risks, analyze performance trends, and support issue resolution to prevent revenue leakage and service disruption.
  • Reporting & Communication: Ensure accurate reporting, clear status updates, and effective issue communication to internal stakeholders and, as appropriate, client contacts.
  • Client Scope: Lead operational work for domestic‑only clients as needed.

Reporting, Trend Monitoring & Continuous Improvement

  • Trend Monitoring & Corrective Action: Review statistical reports and dashboards to identify operational trends, risks, and deficiencies; develop and implement corrective action plans to improve timeliness, quality, and outcomes.
  • Operational Efficiency: Lead tactical efforts to maximize operational efficiency and optimize reimbursement through standardized workflows, issue triage, and collaboration with cross-functional partners.

Client & Stakeholder Relationship Management (Tactical)

  • Liaison & Communication: Act as the primary operational point of contact between facility management and internal teams, ensuring smooth, timely communication and resolution of day-to-day issues.
  • Service Responsiveness & Escalation: Ensure client inquiries are addressed promptly (including providing timelines to resolution), and proactively escalate risks such as unbilled accounts, claim issues, and operational blockers to leadership.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with internal teams (e.g., operations, finance, payer relations, technology, and strategic client management/sales counterparts) to drive resolution and maintain a consistent client experience.
  • Contract Awareness & Compliance: Understand contract terms and ensure operational billing, invoicing, and service delivery remain within negotiated requirements.

Compliance & Professional Standards

  • Regulatory Knowledge: Maintain current knowledge of hospital billing systems, government payer programs, third-party reimbursement policies, and applicable federal/state regulations.
  • Confidentiality: Maintain confidentiality of patient and client information without exception.
  • Continuous Learning & Industry Awareness: Attend required meetings and remain current on industry trends, legislative changes, and best practices.
  • Customer Invoicing & Accuracy: Ensure accuracy of customer invoices and support monthly invoicing processes as required; validate supporting detail and address discrepancies.
  • Management Expectations / Additional Duties: Perform all functions in alignment with management expectations and complete other duties as assigned.

Key Measures of Success

  • Client Retention and Stability
  • Reduction in Client Escalations
  • Cash Performance vs. Goal
  • A/R Days and Denial Trends

Staff Management

Responsible for ensuring area of responsibility has the talent and resources to meet short- and long-term organizational goals as well as ensuring maximum productivity and performance. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Proactively recruit, screen, and select candidates for current and future resource requirements.
  • Effectively orient new hires to ensure a positive and productive employee engagement experience.
  • Ensure structure and hiring plans (within budget) are appropriate for performance and productivity levels required.
  • Utilize the company’s performance management program as designed to align individual performance to overall performance objectives. Meet all completion requirements at a high quality level. Provide ongoing performance feedback. Identify and take appropriate action for non-performance.
  • Ensure each employee has a yearly performance review that is reviewed with employee and the review to be sent to Human Resources each year.

The Equity Compensation Consultant serves as a trusted guide to employee shareholders by delivering personalized education, financial wellness conversations, and support across a wide range of equity compensation plans, including Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), Stock Options, Performance Share Units (PSUs), Stock Appreciation Rights (SARs), and Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPPs). This role helps participants understand, access, and maximize the value of their equity compensation while connecting equity benefits to broader financial wellness goals.

As part of a rapidly growing and evolving team, the Equity Compensation Consultant builds meaningful relationships with shareholders by combining exceptional service with a proactive, consultative approach. Success in this role requires a motivated, growth-oriented professional who identifies opportunities to deepen participant engagement, expands awareness of Empower's financial solutions, and delivers an exceptional shareholder experience while contributing to the continued growth of the business.

We're looking for people to record point-of-view videos of everyday household activities. You mount your smartphone on your head, go about your routine, and the camera captures exactly what you see. These videos help train AI systems and robots to understand how people interact with objects in real-world environments.

Do you wash dishes every day? Vacuum the rug? Walk the dog? Fold laundry? What if you could get paid just for recording it?

  • Record everyday household activities from a first-person perspective — cooking, cleaning, tidying up, folding laundry, gardening, walking the dog, and more
  • Record in your own home, yard, garage, or workspace
  • Follow short recording guidelines per session
  • Upload videos through the project app

jobs.excerpt: Join our team and experience how we lead with passion, positivity, and accountability to deliver the Right Talent.
jobs.description:
Join our team and experience how we lead with passion, positivity, and accountability to deliver the Right Talent. Right Now. We create an environment where you can think big, have fun and truly make a difference.

THE POSITION SUMMARY

The Senior Director / VP, Global Vendor Strategy & Nearshore/Offshore Operations owns the design, governance, and economic performance of Oxford's Associate Vendor (AV) model and its global delivery footprint - encompassing nearshore, offshore, and H-1B supply channels that today support a meaningful and growing share of Oxford's business, but currently operate without a defined structure, consistent contractual treatment, or measured economics.

This role elevates AV from a decentralized, recruiter-managed practice to a strategically governed global program. The mandate spans three distinct use cases - payroll/passthrough, cost-optimized nearshore/offshore and H-1B supply, and nearshore/offshore capability extension - each requiring its own contractual structure, performance standard, and margin profile. At the executive level, this leader is accountable for building Oxford's nearshore/offshore delivery strategy, closing the margin gap between AV and core Oxford delivery, correcting recruiter incentives that currently reward AV placements identically to full-cycle recruiting, and materially reducing the client, legal, and brand risk created by treating fundamentally different vendor relationships as one undifferentiated program.

The scope of this role - governance-only versus governance with delivery-build responsibility - will be finalized alongside Oxford's selected AV operating model direction. This executive will serve as Oxford's internal authority on global delivery economics, offshore/nearshore market dynamics, and vendor partnership strategy.

THE OPPORTUNITY/ KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Vendor Assessment & Segmentation: Lead the strategic assessment, segmentation, and ongoing governance of Oxford's Associate Vendor network - classifying vendors by capability, geography, skillset, and use case (payroll/passthrough, H-1B/offshore supply, nearshore/offshore capability extension). Establish and maintain a tiered, defensible vendor roster that directly supports Oxford's global delivery objectives.
  • Economic & Incentive Alignment: Partner with Sales Compensation and recruiting leadership to review and correct recruiter incentive structures tied to AV usage, with the objective of eliminating rate compression caused by recruiters being paid identically on AV and full-cycle placements.
  • Contractual & Risk Segmentation: Work with Legal to establish distinct contractual frameworks for each AV use case, replacing the current single, undifferentiated agreement structure that treats payroll/passthrough, C2C, and capability-extension relationships the same way.
  • Program Governance: Design and own the enterprise-level governance framework for adding, approving, and exiting Associate Vendors - including standardized due diligence, compliance reviews, onboarding protocols, and performance cadence across onshore, nearshore, and offshore relationships. Ensure governance scales with Oxford's global delivery ambitions.
  • Performance Monitoring: Own the executive-level performance framework covering vendor margin, fill rate, quality, SLA adherence, and rate compression across all delivery channels - onshore, nearshore, and offshore. Deliver regular reporting to senior leadership and ownership that translates vendor economics into business impact.
  • Immigration & Compliance Risk: Serve as Oxford's senior authority on immigration-related vendor risk - owning contractual exposure, compliance monitoring, and policy development for H-1B, OPT/STEM OPT, and nearshore/offshore vendor relationships. Partner with Legal and HR to ensure Oxford's global delivery posture meets regulatory requirements across all operating geographies.
  • Program Optimization: Define and execute Oxford's nearshore and offshore delivery strategy - evaluating market options (India, Philippines, Latin America, Eastern Europe, etc.), selecting and managing strategic delivery partners, and building the operational infrastructure needed to scale offshore/nearshore capacity as a competitive advantage. Own the build-vs.-buy decision framework for nearshore/offshore delivery expansion.
  • Collaboration: Serve as a senior cross-functional partner to Sales, Recruiting, Legal, Finance, and executive leadership - ensuring AV program strategy, offshore/nearshore expansion plans, and vendor economics remain tightly aligned with Oxford's commercial, margin, and growth objectives.
  • Reporting: Deliver executive-level reporting on AV program performance, offshore/nearshore delivery economics, risk exposure, and strategic initiatives - in a format suitable for C-suite and ownership-level review. Translate operational data into strategic recommendations.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE /QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of experience in vendor management, global delivery operations, staffing/recruiting operations, or professional services, with at least 3-5 years in a senior leadership role directly responsible for offshore or nearshore delivery strategy, operations, or vendor programs.
  • Deep expertise in global delivery economics, including bill rate, pay rate, and markup mechanics across W-2, C2C, and 1099 arrangements, with the ability to model, compare, and optimize the cost of delivery across onshore, nearshore, and offshore channels and quantify the margin impact of H-1B versus domestic W-2 supply at scale.
  • Extensive hands-on experience building or managing offshore and nearshore delivery operations, including market selection (India, Philippines, Latin America, Eastern Europe, etc.), vendor partnership structuring, operational setup, and performance management, along with fluency in H-1B, OPT/STEM OPT, and immigration compliance obligations, sponsorship risk, and the contractual distinctions between W-2, C2C, and 1099 arrangements.
  • Demonstrated success building or transforming vendor governance programs at scale, including the design of tiered segmentation models, SLA frameworks, multi-geography onboarding standards, and delivery center operating models that move organizations from informal vendor usage to structured, strategically managed global supply chains.
  • Proven ability to operate as a senior cross-functional executive, influencing Sales, Recruiting, Legal, Finance, and C-suite stakeholders on global delivery strategy, worker classification policy, incentive structure design, and contract frameworks, including the ability to diagnose and correct recruiter pay models that create misaligned incentives around W-2 versus sub-vendor placements.
  • Executive-level analytical fluency - able to build, interpret, and present complex performance, margin, and delivery economics dashboards to C-suite and ownership audiences, and translate data into strategic investment or divestment recommendations.
  • Exceptional leadership presence, executive communication skills, and the ability to manage complex, multi-geography programs across time zones and organizational boundaries.

DESIRED CHARACTERISTICS

  • The ideal candidate will be a decisive, structure-building leader who is comfortable turning an informal, recruiter-managed practice into a disciplined, governed global program, while maintaining the flexibility to adapt the operating model as Oxford's delivery strategy evolves.
  • They will be equally credible in a spreadsheet and in the boardroom - fluent in bill rate, pay rate, and margin mechanics, yet able to translate that economic detail into a clear narrative for C-suite and ownership audiences.
  • This executive must demonstrate sound judgment in balancing competing priorities across sales, legal, compliance, and delivery, correcting misaligned incentives and contractual risk without disrupting the revenue the AV channel currently generates.
  • As a cross-functional leader, they must build trust quickly with Sales, Recruiting, Legal, Finance, and HR, bringing each function along through a period of significant change to how vendor relationships are structured and managed.
  • A reputation for integrity and rigor is essential, as this individual will be Oxford's internal authority on global delivery economics and vendor risk, and must be comfortable delivering direct, data-backed recommendations - including build-vs.-buy and investment/divestment calls - to senior leadership.

EDUCATION

A bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, or a related field required, or equivalent professional experience.
